instruction:
Rewrite `registry/registry.go` whole from the Function Project Registry below. The only change from the current file: the Project struct gains `User string `json:"user"`` (the project's Linux user), between Caps and CreatedAt, and it round-trips through the file like every other field. Every other declaration, sentinel, error text and behaviour stays exactly as the Function states. Do not write or modify any other file.

## Function Project Registry

The registry of projects in one JSON file, rewritten whole and atomically, and a JSON state blob per project.

Behaviour: Declares in registry/registry.go: `var ErrNotFound = errors.New("project not found")`, `var ErrExists = errors.New("project exists")`, `var ErrBadName = errors.New("bad project name")`, `var ErrNoState = errors.New("no state")`, `type Project struct { Name string `json:"name"`; Language string `json:"language"`; RepoURL string `json:"repo_url"`; Dir string `json:"dir"`; Caps queue.Caps `json:"caps"`; User string `json:"user"`; CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"` }`, `type Registry struct` (unexported fields), `func Open(base string) (*Registry, error)`, `func (r *Registry) Base() string`, `func (r *Registry) Add(p Project) error`, `func (r *Registry) Get(name string) (Project, error)`, `func (r *Registry) List() []Project`, `func (r *Registry) SaveState(name string, v any) error` and `func (r *Registry) LoadState(name string, v any) error`. Open creates base (0o700) when missing and reads base/projects.json: missing → empty; not a JSON array of Project → (nil, an error beginning "registry: read "). Add: Name must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ else ErrBadName; a stored name → ErrExists; else stored and the whole list written as a JSON array sorted by Name (json.MarshalIndent with two spaces, an empty list as []) to a temporary file in base then renamed onto projects.json. Get → the project or (Project{}, ErrNotFound). List → a new slice sorted by Name (empty non-nil). SaveState writes json.MarshalIndent(v) to base/<name>/state.json (the directory created 0o700; unknown name → ErrNotFound) by temporary file and rename; LoadState unmarshals it into v, missing file → ErrNoState, unknown name → ErrNotFound. Every error of the file system is returned as is (never one of the sentinels). Values are copies.

Steps:
- produces: Project

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given base := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "state") (missing); when Open(base); List(); Get("demo"); Base(); then a non-nil *Registry, nil; the directory exists; []Project{} (non-nil, empty); (Project{}, ErrNotFound); base
2. given the registry of example 1; Add({Name "zeta", Language "go", RepoURL "https://github.com/o/zeta", Dir "/p/zeta", Caps {30, 3, 5}, CreatedAt 2026-10-08T15:00:00Z}); Add({Name "alpha", Language "python", …, CreatedAt 2026-10-08T15:01:00Z}); when Add twice, then List, then decode base/projects.json; then both nil; List names in order "alpha", "zeta"; the file decodes (json.Unmarshal into []Project) to exactly List(); the directory base holds only projects.json
3. given the registry after example 2; when Add({Name "alpha"}); Add({Name "Alpha"}); Add({Name "-x"}); Add({Name 41 × "a"}); then ErrExists; ErrBadName; ErrBadName; ErrBadName; List still 2
4. given the file written by example 2, Open(base) again; when List; Get("zeta"); then equal field by field to the first registry's List (times round-trip through JSON); Get returns the zeta project
5. given the registry after example 2; type S struct{ N int `json:"n"` }; when SaveState("alpha", S{7}); LoadState("alpha", &out); LoadState("zeta", &out2); SaveState("nope", S{1}); LoadState("nope", &out3); then nil; nil and out == S{7}; ErrNoState; ErrNotFound; ErrNotFound; base/alpha/state.json exists with mode & 0o777 == 0o600 and base/alpha mode & 0o777 == 0o700
6. given base/projects.json holding the text {not json; when Open; then (nil, an error beginning "registry: read ")
7. given the registry of example 1 after Add({Name "alpha", Language "go", Dir "/p/alpha"}); when p := List(); p[0].Name = "changed"; p = append(p, Project{Name: "extra"}); g, _ := Get("alpha"); g.Name = "changed"; then List() and Get("alpha"); then List() is exactly []Project{{Name: "alpha", Language: "go", Dir: "/p/alpha"}} and Get("alpha") returns that project, nil: writes to returned values never reach the registry
8. given the registry of example 1 after Add({Name "zeta", Language "go", Dir "/p/zeta", User "zeta-ux"}); when reopen the base with Open (a second Open of the same base); Get("zeta"); decode base/projects.json with json.Unmarshal into []Project; then Get returns the project with User "zeta-ux", nil; the decoded file equals List() including User "zeta-ux"; a project added without a User (the field the zero string "") still round-trips with User ""

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Claude Behind An Interface: The claude CLI is reached only through claude.Process (stdin lines in, stdout lines out, an exit status); the daemon's tests use claude.Fake fed with lines from tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, never a real claude.
- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.
- Per-User Tokens: Every HTTP / MCP token belongs to one user and sees only that user's projects; only the operator's admin token sees all. Tokens are API keys brought by the user; subscription OAuth tokens are never taken (D5).
- One Chat One User: A Telegram chat maps to at most one user; an unknown chat gets only /start.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token, the Telegram token, claude tokens (subscription OAuth tokens included), API keys, PATs, MCP tokens and one-time links never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.
- Tester Isolation: Every claude session and every git / morph command of a tester's project goes through morph-spawn / morph-run under the project's user; only package claude builds a process argv; no package runs sudo with anything else.

Write the files: `registry/registry.go`.

Go 1.22, the standard library only (go.mod requires nothing; the build runs with GOPROXY=off). gofmt-formatted (gofmt -l prints nothing) and go vet clean. A file's package is its directory's base name; exported names in MixedCaps; a package imports another of the module by the module path of go.mod + "/" + its directory. Tests are `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)` in the package's own `_test.go` files, table tests allowed; compare with `testhelp.Equal(t, what, got, want)` of the module's `internal/testhelp`, never your own helper; no t.Skip, no network, no clock, no goroutine left running.

Read go.mod FIRST (in your context). Every name you need is in them or below; do not invent names, keys or files.

## Function User Registry

The registry of users in one JSON file, rewritten whole and atomically; the token only as a SHA-256 hash.

Behaviour: Declares in users/users.go: `var ErrNotFound = errors.New("user not found")`, `var ErrExists = errors.New("user exists")`, `var ErrBadName = errors.New("bad user name")`, `var ErrChatTaken = errors.New("chat already has a user")`, `type User struct { Name string `json:"name"`; LinuxUser string `json:"linux_user"`; ChatID int64 `json:"chat_id"`; TokenHash string `json:"token_hash"`; CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"` }` (TokenHash is the hex of the SHA-256 of the bearer token, encoding/hex lowercase), `type Users struct` (unexported fields), `func Open(base string, adminToken string) (*Users, error)`, `func (u *Users) Base() string`, `func (u *Users) Add(v User) error`, `func (u *Users) Get(name string) (User, error)`, `func (u *Users) List() []User` and `func (u *Users) Delete(name string) error`. Open creates base (0o700) when missing and reads base/users.json: missing → empty; not a JSON array of User → (nil, an error beginning "users: read "). adminToken "" is allowed (no admin token, IsAdmin always false); a non-empty one is stored as its own SHA-256 hex, never in the clear. Add: Name must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ else ErrBadName; a stored name → ErrExists; a stored user with the same ChatID → ErrChatTaken; else stored and the whole list written as a JSON array sorted by Name (json.MarshalIndent with two spaces, an empty list as []) to a temporary file in base then renamed onto users.json. Get → the user or (User{}, ErrNotFound). List → a new slice sorted by Name (empty non-nil). Delete removes the user and, when it exists, its whole directory base/<name> (os.RemoveAll) and rewrites users.json; unknown name → ErrNotFound. Every error of the file system is returned as is (never one of the sentinels). Values are copies. No error text ever contains a token or its hash.

- produces: User

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given base := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ustate") (missing); when Open(base, ""); List(); Get("alice"); Base(); then a non-nil *Users, nil; the directory exists mode & 0o777 == 0o700; []User{} (non-nil, empty); (User{}, ErrNotFound); base
2. given the registry of example 1; Add({Name "bob", LinuxUser "bob-ux", ChatID 42, TokenHash "a0a996e6da7d3784ee7348bee3e43d60f64b72a3ea18196d9f0fbc99a40a8dbd", CreatedAt 2026-10-12T10:00:00Z}); Add({Name "alice", LinuxUser "alice-ux", ChatID 7, TokenHash "61fdf299956e0522e0a49b4ae572f446b7f811dd73234bc6ddc67aac81d9dcf2", CreatedAt 2026-10-12T10:01:00Z}); when Add twice, then List, then decode base/users.json; then both nil; List names in order "alice", "bob"; the file decodes (json.Unmarshal into []User) to exactly List(); the directory base holds only users.json
3. given the registry after example 2; when Add({Name "alice", LinuxUser "x", ChatID 9, TokenHash "h2"}); Add({Name "carol", LinuxUser "c", ChatID 42, TokenHash "h3"}); Add({Name "Carol"}); Add({Name 41 × "a"}); then ErrExists; ErrChatTaken; ErrBadName; ErrBadName; List still 2
4. given the file written by example 2, Open(base, "admin-op-9") again; when List; Get("bob"); then equal field by field to the first registry's List (times round-trip through JSON); Get returns the bob user
5. given the registry after example 2 with a secret file base/bob/anthropic-key; when Delete("bob"); Get("bob"); os.Stat(base/bob); then nil; (User{}, ErrNotFound); the directory base/bob no longer exists; List holds only alice; Delete("nope") → ErrNotFound
6. given base/users.json holding the text {not json; when Open(base, "x"); then (nil, an error beginning "users: read ")

## Function Token Lookup

A bearer token resolves to exactly one user by a constant-time compare; the operator's admin token resolves to all.

Behaviour: Declares in users/tokens.go, over the Users of users/users.go: `func (u *Users) LookupToken(token string) (User, bool)` and `func (u *Users) IsAdmin(token string) bool`. LookupToken: token "" → (User{}, false); else the SHA-256 hex of token is compared (crypto/subtle. ConstantTimeCompare over the decoded bytes) against every stored TokenHash and the first name-sorted match is returned with true; none → (User{}, false). IsAdmin: token "" → false; a constant-time compare against the admin token hash given to Open (an empty admin token → always false). No error, log or returned text ever contains the token.

Steps:
- calls: User Registry

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given base := a directory with tests/fixtures/users/users-3.json copied as users.json (three users: alice with TokenHash 61fdf299956e0522e0a49b4ae572f446b7f811dd73234bc6ddc67aac81d9dcf2, bob with TokenHash a0a996e6da7d3784ee7348bee3e43d60f64b72a3ea18196d9f0fbc99a40a8dbd, carol with TokenHash b9a24afb8ff6092a52e6232b5b6b76b476503d5322dcdcdf73e75989201448f7); u := Open(base, "admin-op-9"); when LookupToken("tok-bob-2"); LookupToken("tok-alice-1"); LookupToken("tok-carol-3"); then the bob user, true; the alice user, true; the carol user, true (each compared field by field with the decoded fixture)
2. given the registry of example 1; when LookupToken("wrong-token"); LookupToken(""); then (User{}, false); (User{}, false); List is unchanged
3. given the registry of example 1; when IsAdmin("admin-op-9"); IsAdmin("tok-bob-2"); IsAdmin(""); then true; false; false
4. given the registry of example 1 but opened with Open(base, ""); when IsAdmin("admin-op-9"); IsAdmin(""); then false; false (no admin token: IsAdmin is always false, never a panic)

## Function User Secrets

A user's secrets stored as files of mode 0600 that are never returned to a client and never appear in any error text.

Behaviour: Declares in users/secrets.go, over the Users of users/users.go: `var ErrNoSecret = errors.New("no secret")`, `var ErrEmptySecret = errors.New("empty secret")`, `var SecretKinds = []string{"anthropic-key", "github-token"}`, `func (u *Users) SecretPath(name, kind string) string` = filepath.Join(base, name, kind), `func (u *Users) PutSecret(name, kind, value string) error`, `func (u *Users) HasSecret(name, kind string) bool`, `func (u *Users) ReadSecret(name, kind string) (string, error)` and `func (u *Users) DeleteSecret(name, kind string) error`. PutSecret: unknown user → ErrNotFound; kind not in SecretKinds → fmt.Errorf("users: unknown secret kind %q", kind); value "" → ErrEmptySecret; else the user directory is created (0o700) and value is written by a temporary file (0o600) in that directory renamed onto SecretPath; the written file has mode 0o600 even when it existed with another mode. HasSecret: the file exists. ReadSecret: the content verbatim — the value is for morphd's own use only (the claude environment, a credential file); it is never returned to a client and never written to a log, a milestone or an error text; missing → ("", ErrNoSecret); unknown user → ErrNotFound. ## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Claude Behind An Interface: The claude CLI is reached only through claude.Process (stdin lines in, stdout lines out, an exit status); the daemon's tests use claude.Fake fed with lines from tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, never a real claude.
- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.
- Per-User Tokens: Every HTTP / MCP token belongs to one user and sees only that user's projects; only the operator's admin token sees all. Tokens are API keys brought by the user; subscription OAuth tokens are never taken (D5).
- One Chat One User: A Telegram chat maps to at most one user; an unknown chat gets only /start.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token, the Telegram token, claude tokens (subscription OAuth tokens included), API keys, PATs, MCP tokens and one-time links never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.
- Tester Isolation: Every claude session and every git / morph command of a tester's project goes through morph-spawn / morph-run under the project's user; only package claude builds a process argv; no package runs sudo with anything else.
